---
title: "Pillar 4 — Iterative correction and reference handoff"
subtitle: "If targeted correction works once, does repeating it keep working — and can the corrected model hand off to the reference? Two negative results."
---

::: {.question}
[Scientific question]{.pillar-section-label}
If targeted calibration works once, can **repeated xTB queries around the current
transition state** progressively improve the correction further?
:::

## Why we tested it

[Pillar 3](p3-correction.qmd) showed that a single round of barrier-region data brings
the certified corrected saddle to 6.33 kcal/mol against an xTB target of 6.7. The
natural next move is a loop: find the current corrected saddle, ask the reference what
it thinks *there*, add that data, refit, and repeat. If that converged, it would be the
skeleton of a data-efficient calibration workflow.

The loop was run as a **controlled experiment**, not an autonomous system: the query
rule was fixed by hand, and no acquisition function or uncertainty estimate was
involved.

## One iteration

1. Relaxed concerted scan on the current corrected surface → scan barrier, and a seed
   geometry for the saddle search.
2. **Sella** first-order saddle search from that seed.
3. **TS validity gate** — the structure counts as a Diels–Alder saddle only if it
   converged, has exactly one imaginary mode, has forming C–C in 1.5–3.0 Å, and its
   imaginary mode overlaps the forming-bond coordinate by ≥ 0.30.
4. Query GFN2-xTB at that geometry.
5. Build a small local packet — the saddle itself, ±0.05 and ±0.10 Å along the
   imaginary mode, and 2 isotropic 0.05 Å perturbations: **7 new xTB calculations**.
6. Refit the **same** Delta architecture on the cumulative dataset.

Held fixed throughout: the correction architecture and every hyperparameter, and a
48-configuration held-out reactive split that is never trained on.

## Key evidence

Barriers in kcal/mol. "Sella stationary point" is the converged saddle search; it is a
**certified** saddle only when it passes the gate above. Iterations 3 and 5 converged
but had **two** imaginary modes, so their barriers are shown in brackets and are *not*
certified saddle barriers.

[\* xTB R_g from the Phase C reference run used throughout this experiment.]{.table-note}

![Barrier against iteration (frozen-xTB-reactant reference). Iteration 0 is the
closest to the xTB target; the constrained-scan barrier degrades monotonically; circled
points are uncertified.](assets/phase2_barrier.png){width=680}

The [barrier ladder](index.qmd#sec-numbers) shows the same series with the
model-relaxed-reactant reference alongside: it degrades further, from 8.23 to 13.98 at
the last certified iteration.

![TS position oscillates by ±0.5 Å; open circles mark iterations that failed the
saddle-certification gate.](assets/phase2_geometry.png){width=760}

![Held-out reactive error drifts slightly upward while water stays within MD
noise.](assets/phase2_generalization.png){width=760}

::: {.keyresult .caution}
[Key result — negative]{.lbl}
**A strong one-shot correction does not continue improving under repeated local TS
queries with the fixed pairwise Delta architecture.** Iteration 0 was the best model of
the run. Across 5 iterations and **42 additional xTB reference calculations**, the
certified saddle barrier oscillated *away* from the reference — from 6.33 (iteration 0)
to 9.46 kcal/mol at the last certified iteration (4), against the frozen xTB reactant;
8.23 → 13.98 against the model-relaxed reactant — and the constrained-scan barrier
degraded monotonically from 9.87 to 13.91 kcal/mol.
:::

Supporting observations:

- **2 of 6 iterations produced no certifiable first-order saddle** (two imaginary modes),
  and fell back to the scan maximum as the query centre. Their Sella stationary points
  (8.62 and 9.25 kcal/mol) are not counted as certified barriers. (Earlier write-ups
  quoted the error trend as 0.37 → 2.55 kcal/mol; the 2.55 endpoint is iteration 5,
  which is uncertified. The last certified error is 2.76.)
- **Held-out reactive error worsens slightly**: TS+post-TS RMSE 0.6879 → 0.7113 (+3.4%).
  The added data is not generalizing.
- **Water remains stable** — R_g spans 3.690–3.841 Å around the xTB reference of 3.77,
  within per-iteration MD standard deviations of 0.037–0.086 Å, with no condensation.
- **The fit is not diverging.** The Delta coefficient norm stays essentially constant
  (6.05, 5.95, 5.99, 5.97, 5.95, 6.11), so this is a fixed capacity being *reallocated*,
  not a numerically unstable regression.

::: {.methodnote}
[Method control — seeding the saddle search]{.lbl}
An earlier version of this loop seeded each saddle search from the xTB TS, the strategy
that works for *raw* MACE. On a *corrected* surface it fails: Sella converges to a
spurious reactant-basin saddle at 3.20 Å whose imaginary mode is orthogonal to bond
formation (overlap 1.2e−06) and whose "barrier" is −3.84 kcal/mol, below the reactant.
That run is retained as a negative control. The fix — seeding from each iteration's own
relaxed-scan maximum, plus the validity gate above — follows the project's existing
convention for saddle searches.
:::

::: {.methodnote}
[A metric not to over-read]{.lbl}
The cosine between corrected and xTB forces *at a converged saddle* is meaningless: the
corrected force is ~1e−4 eV/Å there by construction, so the cosine is a 0/0 noise ratio.
The interpretable quantity is xTB's **own** residual force at the corrected saddle,
which oscillates over 0.43–2.81 eV/Å with no systematic decrease.
:::

## What we learned

More targeted reference data is **not automatically better** for a fixed correction
architecture — and the corrected model's saddles are not a reliably better handoff
point than a cheap geometric guess. For this system the expensive step is generating a
starting guess, and an IDPP interpolation already does that well. The result is specific and bounded: this correction form, this acquisition
rule, this system, this budget.

Two mechanistic observations point the same direction. The Delta is a sum of *radial*
pair potentials with no angular or many-body terms, while the position and curvature of
a cycloaddition saddle depend on angular reorganization of the forming ring. And xTB is
never near-stationary at the corrected saddle (0.43–2.81 eV/Å), so force-matching there
asks the correction to reproduce a large reference gradient at a point the corrected
model believes is stationary — a directly conflicting demand.

::: {.methodnote}
[What this does and does not claim]{.lbl}
The behaviour is **consistent with a correction-capacity limitation**, which motivates a
controlled capacity ablation. That is a supported hypothesis, not a demonstrated result —
establishing it requires holding the acquisition rule fixed while varying the
correction's expressiveness. This experiment does **not** show that active learning
fails: no acquisition metric, uncertainty estimate, or autonomous sampling was
implemented here.
:::

## Handing off to the reference {#sec-handoff}

If the corrected model cannot be iterated into agreement, can it at least supply a good
*starting point* for the reference's own saddle search — and is there an optimal moment
to hand off? Each corrected-model saddle from the loop above was given to Sella on the
GFN2-xTB surface, and the number of genuine xTB evaluations (`calculate()` calls) needed
to reach the verified xTB TS was counted ([Study 09](09-handoff.qmd)).

| start | xTB calls (total) | reached the xTB TS? |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| xTB-only baseline: relaxed scan → Sella | **582** (547 scan + 35 Sella) | yes |
| handoff from iteration 0 / 1 / 5 | 97 / **50** / 104 | yes |
| handoff from iteration 2 / 3 / 4 | 534 / 452 / 534 | **no** |
| IDPP interpolation, zero prior reference cost | **75** | yes |

[Iterations 2 and 4 reach the right structure but miss the pre-registered
`fmax = 1e−4`; iteration 3 is the only wrong-basin failure ([details](09-handoff.qmd#sec-cost)).]{.table-note}

![Total marginal xTB cost to reach the verified xTB TS, by handoff iteration. Failed
handoffs are crosses; the xTB-only baseline and the IDPP control are horizontal
lines.](assets/aug21_total_cost.png){width=680}

::: {.keyresult .caution}
[Key result — negative]{.lbl}
**Only 3 of 6 handoffs reached the reference TS, with no trend across iterations.** The
best handoff (50 calls) is 11.6× cheaper than the xTB-only baseline, but that baseline
spends 547 of its 582 calls on a relaxed scan that turns out to be unnecessary: a
zero-cost IDPP interpolation guess reaches the same TS in **75** calls. Against that
cheapest working alternative, only one of six handoffs is cheaper — and nothing
identified it in advance. Fewer reference calls in the successful cases do not make the
route reliable.
:::

Every successful run converges to the same structure: forming C–C 2.3153 Å,
6.71 kcal/mol, principal imaginary mode −393.4 cm⁻¹ — the verified xTB TS.

## Is there a handoff signal? {#sec-handoff-diagnostics}

The follow-up asked whether any property of the starting geometry predicts success.
Replicates were run, 14 descriptors were measured for every start, and near-identical
starting points were compared.

![Left: xTB residual force at the handoff geometry does not separate successes from
failures. Right: two near-twin pairs of starting geometries, indistinguishable across
the descriptors, with opposite outcomes.](assets/aug21_descriptor_diagnosis.png){width=760}

::: {.keyresult .caution}
[Key result — negative]{.lbl}
**No tested pre-handoff descriptor reliably predicts success.** Two pairs of starting
geometries separated by only **0.007 Å and 0.022 Å RMSD** produce opposite outcomes,
with 6–12× cost differences. The intuitive rule fails: the start with the *largest* xTB
residual force (IDPP, 4.99 eV/Å) succeeds, while starts with small residual forces
(0.46, 0.69 eV/Å) fail.
:::

- [Demonstrated]{.tag .demo} The qualitative outcome reproduces across replicates;
  successful and stalled cases are deterministic, while one failing case dissociates by
  different routes in each replicate (a flat, dissociative surface amplifying bit-level
  SCF differences).
- [Interpretation]{.tag .interp} At the resolution that separates these candidates, the
  handoff outcome does not behave as a smooth function of the starting state.

## Next question

**Is correction-model capacity the bottleneck?** The discriminating experiment holds the
acquisition rule fixed and varies expressiveness — angular or three-body terms, a larger
cutoff, more radial channels. If a richer correction converges on the same 42-query
budget, the ceiling is architectural and an acquisition metric becomes worth building.
If it does not, no acquisition function would rescue the loop.
